investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T04:17–04:24Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. Only 2 nodes carry this resource; both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time, and preemption found no victims to evict. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent identity or VM reference, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the eval to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck 146s, latencyMs=151556 — confirms the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 143s, latencyMs=151805 — a third independent pod also failed to schedule, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent because the pod never started and createAgent() never returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required:true with degradedAfterFailures:1, meaning a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource pool exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads are holding all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across a ~7-minute window.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node selector that only matches 2 of 6 nodes, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes. If the selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, capacity that was previously spread across more nodes is now constrained to 2. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this as a recent regression, but it cannot be ruled out.

TERTIARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota set too low for the cluster size: the extended resource may be configured with a low advertised capacity per node (e.g., 1 or 2 slots), and concurrent eval runs or background workloads saturate it quickly. Preemption finding zero victims suggests no lower-priority pods are present to evict, consistent with all slots being held by equal- or higher-priority workloads.

QUATERNARY — withCleanup() in run-status-probes.mjs not releasing VM resources from a prior failed run: if a previous eval run left a pod or VM resource allocated without cleanup, the slot would remain consumed. The verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, so no prior run history is available to confirm or deny this.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-07T04:19–04:24Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~135–146 s), preventing the eval runner from ever reaching the state-polling phase. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the remote-agent VM node pool, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting real infrastructure unavailability.

Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for 135–146 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T04:17–04:24Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. Only 2 nodes carry this resource; both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time, and preemption found no victims to evict. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent identity or VM reference, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the eval to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=140675, pod stuck unscheduled for 135s before the check timed out as fail.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck 146s, latencyMs=151556 — confirms the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 143s, latencyMs=151805 — a third independent pod also failed to schedule, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent because the pod never started and createAgent() never returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod is unschedulable this call cannot complete and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required:true with degradedAfterFailures:1, meaning a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource pool exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads are holding all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across a ~7-minute window.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node selector that only matches 2 of 6 nodes, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes. If the selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, capacity that was previously spread across more nodes is now constrained to 2. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this as a recent regression, but it cannot be ruled out.

TERTIARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota set too low for the cluster size: the extended resource may be configured with a low advertised capacity per node (e.g., 1 or 2 slots), and concurrent eval runs or background workloads saturate it quickly. Preemption finding zero victims suggests no lower-priority pods are present to evict, consistent with all slots being held by equal- or higher-priority workloads.

QUATERNARY — withCleanup() in run-status-probes.mjs not releasing VM resources from a prior failed run: if a previous eval run left a pod or VM resource allocated without cleanup, the slot would remain consumed. The verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, so no prior run history is available to confirm or deny this.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-07T04:19–04:24Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~135–146 s), preventing the eval runner from ever reaching the state-polling phase. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the remote-agent VM node pool, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting real infrastructure unavailability.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 04:19 and 04:24 UTC on 2026-07-07 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and no runtime evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever produced, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 nodes that support that resource type. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) attempts to schedule a remote agent pod using kata peer-pods isolation; at the time of the run, 0 of 6 nodes could satisfy the scheduling request — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for 135–146 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval pod. All three sibling checks show the same error within a ~5-minute window, consistent with sustained resource saturation rather than a transient blip.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible for kata peer-pods scheduling. If those 2 nodes are small or heavily loaded, the effective capacity ceiling is very low and easily exhausted.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for remote agent workloads: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the cluster may be insufficient to handle concurrent eval runs plus any live remote agent workloads, causing contention.

Lower probability — transient scheduling anomaly: a brief spike in remote agent pod demand (e.g., from a prior eval run that did not clean up) could have temporarily consumed all VM slots; this would be disproved if the eval passes on re-run.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-runtime shortly after this failure with no cluster changes would suggest the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.
kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes showing available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the failure would disprove the resource exhaustion hypothesis.

Evidence that the pod scheduling error message was produced by a misconfigured resource request in the eval runner (e.g., requesting more VM slots than exist) rather than actual capacity exhaustion would shift the cause to an eval configuration bug.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state from a different environment or time window would indicate the issue is environment-specific or time-bounded rather than a persistent cluster capacity problem.
Evidence that the node affinity/selector on the pod was recently changed and now excludes nodes that previously matched would point to a configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability on eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a scheduling timeout buried in the agent lifecycle eval.

Add a cluster node affinity/selector health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's scheduling constraints, alerting early if the eligible node pool shrinks below a safe threshold.

Add a stuck-pod detection eval that scans for remote agent pods in Pending/Unschedulable state older than a configurable threshold, enabling faster detection of scheduling failures independent of the full agent lifecycle eval.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling check within the remote-agent-create eval that distinguishes 'pod scheduling failed' from 'pod scheduled but agent did not become ready', so the failure message and evidence can be more precisely categorized.
